sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金（Andrew Ross Sorkin）。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日通讯《Dealbook》报道商业与政策新闻。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 Dealbook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯（Vance）、埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zoran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德（Lagarde）、佐兰·蒙达尼（Zoran Mondani）以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 届时，你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分精选访谈，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: 18th.
If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Sam Anderson, and I am a staff writer for the New York Times Magazine, which normally means I spend many weeks or many months doing deep reporting on subjects and writing
sentences.zh: 你好，我是萨姆·安德森（Sam Anderson），是《纽约时报杂志》的特约撰稿人。这通常意味着我需要花费数周甚至数月的时间对主题进行深度报道，并撰写

sentences.en: about everything from the fragile ankles of Michelangelo's David to profiles of basketball
sentences.zh: 从米开朗基罗《大卫》雕像脆弱的脚踝，到篮球

sentences.en: stars like Russell Westbrook, or more recently, a profile of Weird Al Yankovic that you may remember from a few weeks ago.
sentences.zh: 明星（如拉塞尔·威斯布鲁克）的人物专访，或者最近那篇你可能在几周前读过的关于“怪人奥尔”扬科维奇（Weird Al Yankovic）的专访等各种题材。

sentences.en: But I've also helped to develop this column that appears every week in the magazine, which is called Letter of Recommendation.
sentences.zh: 但我还协助开发了杂志每周刊登的一个专栏，名为“推荐信”（Letter of Recommendation）。

sentences.en: I always get credit for inventing letter of recommendation, but I really have to give the credit to my wife, Sarah, who came up with it
sentences.zh: 人们总是把发明“推荐信”专栏的功劳归于我，但我真的必须把这份功劳归于我的妻子萨拉（Sarah）。那是有一天，我一直在喋喋不休地念叨着我有多么欣赏林赛·

sentences.en: one day when I was going on and on and on about how wonderful I found the guitar solos of Lindsay
sentences.zh: 白金汉（Lindsay Buckingham）的吉他独奏，他是弗利特伍德麦克合唱团（Fleetwood Mac）的词曲作者兼吉他手。

sentences.en: Buckingham, the songwriter and guitarist for Fleetwood Mac.
sentences.zh: 我就是停不下来。

sentences.en: I just wouldn't stop.
sentences.zh: 我就是停不下来。

sentences.en: And she, I think, in like self-defense said, hey, why don't you have a column where you can just pour out your deep,
sentences.zh: 我想她是出于自卫，随口说了一句：嘿，你为什么不开个专栏，把你对世界上各种事物的深沉、

sentences.en: happy love of various things in the world, and then you wouldn't have to say them out loud to me ever.
sentences.zh: 快乐的爱都倾泻出来，这样你就不用再对着我大声说了。

sentences.en: And right then I remember thinking, yeah, I could call it Letter of Recommendation and just
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，我记得我心想，没错，我可以把它叫作“推荐信”，然后

sentences.en: like really go crazy with enthusiasm for some thing out in the world, and it could be absolutely anything.
sentences.zh: 真的可以对世界上某样东西疯狂地表达热情，而且可以是任何东西。

sentences.en: And in the years since, it was six years ago now, it's really just expanded and expanded,
sentences.zh: 从那以后的几年里——现在已经是六年了——它真的不断扩展，不断壮大，

sentences.en: and it's brought in all these voices that I could never have predicted writing about all these subjects that I would never have thought to write about.
sentences.zh: 它引入了许多我从未预料到的声音，写下了许多我从未想过要写的主题。

sentences.en: That's kind of the beauty of it is
sentences.zh: 这就是它的美妙之处，

sentences.en: it's this incredible diversity of joy and enthusiasm.
sentences.zh: 它汇聚了令人难以置信的快乐与热情的多样性。

sentences.en: I think the best columns are the ones that start with a subject that seems pretty straightforward, but then kind of overflow
sentences.zh: 我认为最好的专栏文章，往往是从一个看似非常简单的主题开始，然后逐渐溢出

sentences.en: the boundaries of that subject and turn into something really revealing and personal about the writer.
sentences.zh: 该主题的边界，转而变成关于作者本人非常深刻且私人的揭示。

sentences.en: There've been letters of recommendation about like bunk beds and crickets and hangovers and just things that you would never, ever expect someone to recommend to you.
sentences.zh: 曾经有关于双层床、蟋蟀、宿醉的“推荐信”，都是你绝对想不到会有人向你推荐的东西。

sentences.en: I guess one way to say that would be, here goes my dogs.
sentences.zh: 我想换种说法就是，我的狗来了。

sentences.en: Letter of Recommendation, yelling at your dog for barking all day long.
sentences.zh: “推荐信”：因为你的狗整天叫个不停而对它大吼大叫。

sentences.en: That's my little wiener dog.
sentences.zh: 那是我的小腊肠犬。

sentences.en: His name is Walnut.
sentences.zh: 它的名字叫核桃（Walnut）。

sentences.en: Walnut, that's enough, buddy.
sentences.zh: 核桃，够了，伙计。

sentences.en: We heard you.
sentences.zh: 我们听见你叫了。

sentences.en: I think my wife may be just arriving back home, so he'll bark for a minute.
sentences.zh: 我想我妻子可能刚到家，所以它会再叫一会儿。

sentences.en: So here are three Letter of Recommendation columns from the last several years that might help you find a little bit of distraction and also maybe a little meaning
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有三篇过去几年里的“推荐信”专栏，或许能帮你找到一点消遣，也可能在

sentences.en: in this time when we're all looking for those things.
sentences.zh: 我们都在寻找这些东西的时刻，为你带来一点意义。

sentences.en: Letter of Recommendation
sentences.zh: 推荐信

sentences.en: Grandma's Teenage Diaries
sentences.zh: 奶奶的少女日记

sentences.en: Written by David Reese
sentences.zh: 作者：大卫·里斯（David Reese）

sentences.en: Read by Eduardo Ballerini
sentences.zh: 朗读：爱德华多·巴莱里尼（Eduardo Ballerini）

sentences.en: My parents recently found five journals in one of those listless cardboard boxes that leaves an attic only when somebody dies or the house is sold.
sentences.zh: 我父母最近在那些只有在某人去世或房子卖掉时才会从阁楼里搬出来的杂乱纸箱中，发现了五本日志。

sentences.en: Don't worry, everyone survived the sale of the house.
sentences.zh: 别担心，大家都挺过了卖房这件事。

sentences.en: The journals were written by my paternal grandmother when she was living with her widowed mom in Gloversville, New York.
sentences.zh: 这些日志是我祖母在纽约州格洛弗斯维尔（Gloversville）与她守寡的母亲同住时写的。

sentences.en: It was July 1910.
sentences.zh: 那是1910年7月。

sentences.en: She was 16, an only child.
sentences.zh: 她当时16岁，是独生女。

sentences.en: The first entry begins, Dearest Anybody, which I took as permission to start reading.
sentences.zh: 第一篇日记开头写着“亲爱的任何人”，我把它当作了开始阅读的许可。

sentences.en: Each of my grandmothers died before I was born.
sentences.zh: 我的祖母们在我出生前就都去世了。

sentences.en: I've seen a few austere photographs, but I don't know what their voices sounded like or how they moved through a room.
sentences.zh: 我见过几张严肃的照片，但我不知道她们的声音听起来是什么样，也不知道她们在房间里走动时是什么样子。

sentences.en: My family is small, and its history has never been part of my identity.
sentences.zh: 我的家庭很小，其历史从未成为我身份的一部分。

sentences.en: I can probably name more ex-members of Black Flag than I can Reese's ancestors.
sentences.zh: 我能叫出的“黑旗乐队”（Black Flag）前成员的名字，可能比我能叫出的里斯家族祖先的名字还要多。

sentences.en: I assumed being disconnected from the past was just part of the modern condition, a liberating byproduct of cosmopolitanism.
sentences.zh: 我曾以为与过去脱节只是现代生活的一部分，是世界主义的一种解放副产品。

sentences.en: Well, the modern condition is a scam.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现代生活就是一个骗局。

sentences.en: Leafing through your family's antique media makes every subsequent moment spent clicking through social media feel like saccharine connectivity, a feast of empty calories.
sentences.zh: 翻阅你家族的古董媒介，会让随后花在点击社交媒体上的每一刻都显得像是糖精般的虚假连接，一场空洞热量的盛宴。

sentences.en: We should smash our computers and throw our phones into the ocean, then open every cardboard box in every attic on earth and read whatever falls out.
sentences.zh: 我们应该砸碎电脑，把手机扔进大海，然后打开地球上每一个阁楼里的每一个纸箱，阅读掉出来的任何东西。

sentences.en: These are the most euphoric books I've ever read.
sentences.zh: 这是我读过最令人陶醉的书。

sentences.en: At first I could handle only a few pages each night.
sentences.zh: 起初，我每晚只能读几页。

sentences.en: The experience was just too intense, provoking in me an ecstatic, wandering melancholy and a familial pride that felt both intimate and alien.
sentences.zh: 这种体验太强烈了，在我心中激起了一种狂喜而游离的忧郁，以及一种既亲密又陌生的家族自豪感。

sentences.en: My grandmother finally came rushing into my life with an adolescent, whooping vitality that felt as if it had been building for the entire century since
sentences.zh: 我的祖母终于带着一种青春的、欢呼雀跃的活力冲进了我的生活，感觉就像是自她

sentences.en: her diaries had last been open.
sentences.zh: 日记最后一次被打开后的整个世纪里，这种活力一直在积聚。

sentences.en: I assumed the diaries would be dark, astringent and antiquated, like sipping vinegar through an iron lung.
sentences.zh: 我原以为这些日记会是阴暗、尖刻且陈旧的，就像透过铁肺喝醋一样。

sentences.en: But my grandmother had as much fun as any molly gobbler at Coachella.
sentences.zh: 但我的祖母玩得比科切拉音乐节（Coachella）上的任何年轻人都要开心。

sentences.en: She records three primary passions, eating ice cream.
sentences.zh: 她记录了三大爱好：吃冰淇淋。

sentences.en: In the afternoon we had ice cream.
sentences.zh: 下午我们吃了冰淇淋。

sentences.en: Oh, delicious memory.
sentences.zh: 哦，美味的记忆。

sentences.en: Going to church.
sentences.zh: 去教堂。

sentences.en: The minister preached on cheerfulness and it was awfully good.
sentences.zh: 牧师讲了关于快乐的布道，非常好。

sentences.en: And singing with her friends.
sentences.zh: 还有和朋友们唱歌。

sentences.en: That is, when they weren't laid up with the mumps or the grip or any of those other mysterious old-timey diseases.
sentences.zh: 当然，是在她们没有因为腮腺炎、流感或任何其他神秘的旧时代疾病而卧床不起的时候。

sentences.en: But my teenage grandmother's great genius was flirting.
sentences.zh: 但我那十几岁的祖母最大的天赋是调情。

sentences.en: Those amazing boys.
sentences.zh: 那些了不起的男孩们。

sentences.en: The peachy, dandy, charming boys of Gloversville, anointed with adjectives now reserved for Yelp reviews of bed and breakfasts.
sentences.zh: 格洛弗斯维尔那些桃子般甜美、时髦、迷人的男孩们，被冠以现在只用于点评民宿的形容词。

sentences.en: I can barely keep up with her crushes or their fluctuations in status.
sentences.zh: 我几乎跟不上她迷恋的对象，也跟不上他们地位的波动。

sentences.en: But what do you suppose Peggy told me?
sentences.zh: 但你猜佩吉（Peggy）跟我说了什么？

sentences.en: That Bill was mad at me because he thought I was mad at him because he talked to Velma Thorne.
sentences.zh: 比尔（Bill）生我的气，因为他以为我生他的气，因为他跟维尔玛·索恩（Velma Thorne）说话了。

sentences.en: And there I didn't even know he had been talking to her.
sentences.zh: 而我甚至都不知道他跟她说过话。

sentences.en: Wasn't it funny?
sentences.zh: 这难道不滑稽吗？

sentences.en: So I told Ralph to tell Bill I wasn't mad and it didn't bother me how much he talked to Velma.
sentences.zh: 所以我告诉拉尔夫（Ralph）去告诉比尔，我没生气，他跟维尔玛说多少话我都不介意。

sentences.en: It turns out poor Bill, being stout and a cigarette bummer, I hate to see a fellow smoke when he's with a girl on the street, don't you?
sentences.zh: 事实证明，可怜的比尔，又胖又爱蹭烟抽——我讨厌看到男人在街上和女孩在一起时抽烟，你不讨厌吗？

sentences.en: Was no match for Grant.
sentences.zh: 根本比不上格兰特（Grant）。

sentences.en: Or Jonesy.
sentences.zh: 或者琼斯（Jonesy）。

sentences.en: Or the mysterious Sunshine, who if my grandmother is to be believed, was for one summer in 1911 the most alluring young man in the universe.
sentences.zh: 又或者是神秘的“阳光”（Sunshine），如果我祖母的话可信的话，他在1911年的那个夏天是宇宙中最迷人的年轻人。

sentences.en: One grand rower, fisher, and sportsman.
sentences.zh: 一位伟大的划船手、垂钓者和运动员。

sentences.en: Really, I never saw anybody like him.
sentences.zh: 真的，我从未见过像他这样的人。

sentences.en: Emma and I are both dippy over him.
sentences.zh: 艾玛（Emma）和我都为他神魂颠倒。

sentences.en: Arguments with adults are referred to but never detailed.
sentences.zh: 她提到了与大人的争吵，但从未详述。

sentences.en: She doesn't resent her mother's discipline, even when she gets a lovely scolding for finishing someone else's ice cream.
sentences.zh: 她并不怨恨母亲的管教，即使是因为吃光了别人的冰淇淋而受到可爱的责骂时也是如此。

sentences.en: In contrast, I used my own teenage diary as a petri dish for cultivating ever more potent strains of bitterness, in part through recording every injustice I suffered.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，我把自己十几岁的日记当作培养更强烈苦涩感的培养皿，部分原因是我记录了自己遭受的每一件不公。

sentences.en: We're having a party in Latin tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 我们明天要在拉丁语课上开派对。

sentences.en: I got mad at mom because she only got normal chips.
sentences.zh: 我生妈妈的气，因为她只买了普通的薯片。

sentences.en: She said everyone likes normal, plain chips.
sentences.zh: 她说大家都喜欢普通的、原味的薯片。

sentences.en: I mouthed off at her.
sentences.zh: 我顶撞了她。

sentences.en: I like to think my teenage grandmother's superior personality was due to her being 16 before the invention of cool as a virtue, or even for that matter, teenager as an identity.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢认为我那十几岁祖母优越的性格，是因为她在“酷”作为一种美德被发明出来之前就已经16岁了，甚至就“青少年”作为一个身份而言也是如此。

sentences.en: Being surly is a challenge if it's not expected of you, or if you're too busy eating ice cream to bother.
sentences.zh: 如果你不被期待变得乖戾，或者如果你忙着吃冰淇淋而没空理会，那么变得乖戾就是一种挑战。

sentences.en: I also acknowledge that she was subjectively a better teenager.
sentences.zh: 我也承认，从主观上讲，她是一个更好的青少年。

sentences.en: I haven't finished reading the diaries.
sentences.zh: 我还没读完这些日记。

sentences.en: I don't want to be done.
sentences.zh: 我不想读完。

sentences.en: But my favorite passage so far, the one that finally made me cry, was this, recorded in a moment's happy aftermath and left as an unwitting legacy.
sentences.zh: 但我目前最喜欢的一段，也是最终让我落泪的一段，是记录在一段快乐余波中的文字，并作为一份无心的遗产留了下来。

sentences.en: It was a Monday evening in 1911, near the end of summer.
sentences.zh: 那是1911年的一个周一晚上，夏末时分。

sentences.en: My grandmother was sitting on the porch with friends after dining on egg sandwiches, pickles, pickles, and peaches and cream.
sentences.zh: 我祖母和朋友们在吃完鸡蛋三明治、腌菜、腌菜，还有桃子奶油后，坐在门廊上。

sentences.en: Delicious.
sentences.zh: 美味。

sentences.en: A neighbor started playing a hand organ.
sentences.zh: 一位邻居开始弹奏手摇风琴。

sentences.en: The music was irresistible.
sentences.zh: 音乐让人无法抗拒。

sentences.en: The girls flew across the street to listen.
sentences.zh: 女孩们飞奔过马路去听。

sentences.en: And when the neighbor started up with, put your arms around me, honey, something magical happened.
sentences.zh: 当邻居开始演奏《亲爱的，搂住我》（Put Your Arms Around Me, Honey）时，奇妙的事情发生了。

sentences.en: We all began to dance, right on the street.
sentences.zh: 我们都开始跳舞，就在街上。

sentences.en: The people on the corner were dancing on their porch, and we couldn't help ourselves.
sentences.zh: 街角的人们在他们的门廊上跳舞，我们情不自禁。

sentences.en: Eventually, the dancers stood still in the evening air to catch their breath.
sentences.zh: 最终，舞者们在晚风中静止下来，喘口气。

sentences.en: We all felt so sweet and nice.
sentences.zh: 我们都感到如此甜蜜和美好。

sentences.en: And then, just when my teenage grandmother thought things couldn't get any sweeter, Harvey walked by.
sentences.zh: 然后，就在我那十几岁的祖母以为事情不可能再甜蜜的时候，哈维（Harvey）走了过来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果可以免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获得30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: Letter of Recommendation
sentences.zh: 推荐信

sentences.en: Superstitions
sentences.zh: 迷信

sentences.en: Written by Karen Russell
sentences.zh: 作者：凯伦·罗素（Karen Russell）

sentences.en: Read by Samantha Dez
sentences.zh: 朗读：萨曼莎·德兹（Samantha Dez）

sentences.en: Hey, a new acquaintance said to me shortly after I moved to Portland, Oregon.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我搬到俄勒冈州波特兰市不久后，一位新认识的人对我说。

sentences.en: I think I saw you running by the river yesterday.
sentences.zh: 我想我昨天看到你在河边跑步了。

sentences.en: He was frowning a little, as if fact-checking the memory.
sentences.zh: 他皱着眉头，好像在核实记忆的真实性。

sentences.en: Did you jump up like Michael Jordan to touch a leaf?
sentences.zh: 你是不是像迈克尔·乔丹一样跳起来去摸一片叶子？

sentences.en: Indeed, I had.
sentences.zh: 确实，我做了。

sentences.en: I was aghast that this had been visible at rush hour from NATO Parkway.
sentences.zh: 我感到震惊，因为在高峰时段从北约公园大道（NATO Parkway）竟然能看到这一幕。

sentences.en: Nobody wants to be spotted in mesh shorts, certainly not while petitioning a birch for luck.
sentences.zh: 没人想被看到穿着网眼短裤，更不用说是在向一棵桦树祈求好运时。

sentences.en: I was probably stretching, I offered.
sentences.zh: 我可能是在拉伸，我解释道。

sentences.en: Yeah, he said doubtfully.
sentences.zh: 是吗，他怀疑地说。

sentences.en: It really looked like you were high-fiving a tree.
sentences.zh: 看起来你真的在和一棵树击掌。

sentences.en: A few months later, at the Oaks Bottom Wildlife Refuge, a friend waved me over.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，在橡树底野生动物保护区（Oaks Bottom Wildlife Refuge），一位朋友向我招手。

sentences.en: Hey, I thought that was you.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我以为那是你。

sentences.en: Were you praying back there?
sentences.zh: 你在后面祈祷吗？

sentences.en: She'd seen me kneeling in mud, touching a solar yellow dandelion.
sentences.zh: 她看到我跪在泥地里，触摸着一朵太阳黄色的蒲公英。

sentences.en: Yes, I said, to expedite my day, because this seemed less bonkers than explaining what I was actually doing.
sentences.zh: 是的，我说，为了让这一天过得快点，因为这似乎比解释我到底在做什么要正常得多。

sentences.en: Touching leaves and flowers for luck, which I've done since earliest childhood.
sentences.zh: 触摸叶子和花朵祈求好运，这是我从童年早期就开始做的事情。

sentences.en: Superstitious people are often dismissed as irrational, stunted thinkers.
sentences.zh: 迷信的人常被视为非理性的、思维迟钝的人。

sentences.en: Mental children who never outgrow a scrambled understanding of causality.
sentences.zh: 那些从未摆脱对因果关系混乱理解的精神上的孩子。

sentences.en: Even though studies that confirm improved performance for superstitious athletes can sound patronizing,
sentences.zh: 尽管那些证实迷信运动员表现有所提升的研究听起来可能带有屈尊俯就的意味，

sentences.en: hypothesizing that rituals like Serena Williams' five bounces before her first serve work by conferring the illusion of control.
sentences.zh: 假设像塞雷娜·威廉姆斯（Serena Williams）发球前拍球五次这样的仪式，是通过赋予控制的错觉来起作用的。

sentences.en: To the skeptical observer, superstitions must look like blind adherence to a stupid rule, an automated naivete.
sentences.zh: 对于怀疑论者来说，迷信一定看起来像是对愚蠢规则的盲目遵守，一种自动化的天真。

sentences.en: And I'll admit that several of my own feel less like a conscious act than a fearful reflex.
sentences.zh: 我承认，我自己的几个迷信行为感觉更像是恐惧的反射，而不是有意识的行为。

sentences.en: I recently bought an extra Coke Zero to avoid a $6.66 charge.
sentences.zh: 我最近多买了一瓶零度可乐，以避免6.66美元的收费。

sentences.en: Stand down, Satan.
sentences.zh: 退下吧，撒旦。

sentences.en: But those of us who carry charms and sidestep ladders will tell you that superstitions can have an undeniable power.
sentences.zh: 但我们这些随身携带护身符、绕过梯子的人会告诉你，迷信确实拥有一种不可否认的力量。

sentences.en: Not because they change the future, but because they articulate a wish.
sentences.zh: 并非因为它们能改变未来，而是因为它们表达了一种愿望。

sentences.en: Superstitions are a special syntax, the ellipses we use to bridge the present and the dreamed-of future.
sentences.zh: 迷信是一种特殊的句法，是我们用来连接现实与梦想未来的省略号。

sentences.en: Humble, hopeful, fearful, human.
sentences.zh: 谦卑、充满希望、心怀恐惧，这就是人性。

sentences.en: My dad, a Navy veteran, and the most superstitious person I know, would throw salt over his shoulder to reverse bad luck, occasionally hitting a Denny's waiter in the face.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是一位海军退伍军人，也是我认识的人中最迷信的一个。他会把盐撒过肩头来扭转霉运，偶尔还会撒到丹尼餐厅服务员的脸上。

sentences.en: Don't worry, kids, he would call out as he went diving into the bushes to avoid an inky kitten.
sentences.zh: “别担心，孩子们，”他会一边喊着，一边冲进灌木丛，以避开一只黑猫。

sentences.en: I saw a little gray around the paws.
sentences.zh: 我看到它的爪子周围有一点灰色。

sentences.en: From him, I learned that superstitions can be a form of prayer, as well as an exorcism in miniature.
sentences.zh: 从他身上，我了解到迷信既可以是一种祈祷，也可以是一种微型的驱魔仪式。

sentences.en: You release the fear that comes from feeling responsible for everything that happens to you, an especially American delusion.
sentences.zh: 你释放了那种因觉得自己对所发生的一切负有责任而产生的恐惧，这是一种典型的美国式错觉。

sentences.en: You acknowledge the mysterious convergence of forces sustaining you, and you make your humble petition for more of the same.
sentences.zh: 你承认支撑你的力量存在着神秘的汇合，并为你想要更多同样的眷顾而谦卑地祈求。

sentences.en: More light, more love, more life.
sentences.zh: 更多的光明，更多的爱，更多的生命。

sentences.en: Safe passage to the next moment and the one after that.
sentences.zh: 平安度过此刻，以及接下来的每一刻。

sentences.en: After Hurricane Andrew destroyed our home in 1992, a nine-foot storm surge seemed to choose us, leaving the other houses on our block largely untouched.
sentences.zh: 1992年安德鲁飓风摧毁了我们的家园，九英尺高的风暴潮似乎选中了我们，而我们街区的其他房子却基本完好无损。

sentences.en: I developed a repertoire of new superstitions overnight, like mental mushrooms sprouting out of the salt water that had flooded up to our ceiling.
sentences.zh: 我一夜之间发展出一套新的迷信，就像从淹没到天花板的盐水中长出的精神蘑菇。

sentences.en: These feral rituals compelled me to pay a kind of exegetical attention to the sky and the sea, to look for signs of mercy in the natural world.
sentences.zh: 这些野性的仪式迫使我以一种诠释性的关注去审视天空和海洋，在自然界中寻找仁慈的迹象。

sentences.en: They felt authorless and calmed me.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎没有作者，却让我平静下来。

sentences.en: Cross yourself if you see the white heron on mile marker number seven.
sentences.zh: 如果你在七号里程碑看到白鹭，就画个十字祈祷。

sentences.en: Pause on your bicycle to touch the lucky hibiscus, moon blue inside its orange petals.
sentences.zh: 骑车时停下来摸摸那株幸运的木槿花，它橙色的花瓣里透着月光般的蓝色。

sentences.en: When the hurricane set off a domino rally of misfortune in our family, I thought we must be cursed.
sentences.zh: 当飓风在我们家引发了一连串不幸的多米诺骨牌效应时，我以为我们一定是被诅咒了。

sentences.en: Through the cracked binoculars of childhood, I filtered events into rewards and punishments.
sentences.zh: 透过童年那副破裂的双筒望远镜，我将发生的事件过滤为奖励和惩罚。

sentences.en: But my father returned from volunteer work at the Homestead FEMA trailers, with stories of families scattered to the winds without a stick of luck,
sentences.zh: 但父亲从霍姆斯特德联邦紧急事务管理局拖车区的志愿者工作回来后，带回了许多家庭流离失所、毫无运气的故事，

sentences.en: which in America is synonymous with money in the bank.
sentences.zh: 而在美国，运气往往等同于银行里的存款。

sentences.en: Will touching a leaf or carrying a charm bend reality?
sentences.zh: 触摸一片叶子或携带一个护身符就能扭转现实吗？

sentences.en: Disperse the storm before it makes landfall, or, failing that, ensure that a net will catch and hold you?
sentences.zh: 在风暴登陆前驱散它，或者如果做不到，确保有一张网能接住并托住你？

sentences.en: Certainly not.
sentences.zh: 当然不能。

sentences.en: That net simply does not exist for millions of people in this country, and superstitions won't weave it into existence.
sentences.zh: 对于这个国家的数百万人来说，那张网根本不存在，而迷信也无法将其编织出来。

sentences.en: What these ritual acknowledgments of life's precariousness can do is wake you up to the breath filling your lungs and the sun on your face,
sentences.zh: 这些对生命不确定性的仪式性承认所能做的，是让你意识到肺部的呼吸和脸上的阳光，

sentences.en: To that antiquated binary of good and bad, I would add strange luck.
sentences.zh: 对于好与坏这种陈旧的二元对立，我想再加上一种：奇怪的运气。

sentences.en: Here we find ourselves, after all, hurtling through space-time together on this weird spinning rock.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，我们正一起在这颗奇怪的旋转岩石上，在时空中疾驰。

sentences.en: In the aftermath of the hurricane, I needed superstitions to remind me that we are buoyed on the mothership, with a consciousness that can imagine its way into the future.
sentences.zh: 飓风过后，我需要迷信来提醒我，我们正漂浮在母舰上，拥有着能够想象未来的意识。

sentences.en: Touching the blue swirl inside the blossoming hibiscus, I remembered how little was mine to control.
sentences.zh: 触摸着盛开的木槿花中那抹蓝色的漩涡，我记起自己能控制的东西是多么微不足道。

sentences.en: I felt free to move into an unknown future, carefully, and even hopefully, having just connected with another life form that was flourishing against some astronomically long odds.
sentences.zh: 我感到可以自由地迈向未知的未来，小心翼翼，甚至充满希望，因为我刚刚与另一种在极其渺茫的几率中茁壮成长的生命形式建立了联系。

sentences.en: Fear does animate certain superstitions, but even this becomes a kind of thanksgiving.
sentences.zh: 恐惧确实激发了某些迷信，但即使是这种恐惧也变成了一种感恩。

sentences.en: Flip the coin of fear, and you rediscover the everything you have to lose.
sentences.zh: 翻转恐惧的硬币，你会重新发现你所拥有的一切是多么值得珍惜。

sentences.en: The one fate we all share is so overwhelming that we need to carry it together, the pallbearers of a terrible, heavy certainty.
sentences.zh: 我们共同面对的唯一命运是如此沉重，以至于我们需要一起承担，作为一种可怕而沉重必然性的抬棺人。

sentences.en: Superstitions might not ward off suffering and death, but they can draw a dream into focus.
sentences.zh: 迷信或许无法抵御苦难和死亡，但它们能让梦想变得清晰。

sentences.en: Our baby daughter is due this August, I have finally been able to tell people, after the tenuous early months when this felt unutterable.
sentences.zh: 我们的女儿预产期在今年八月，在经历了最初几个月那种感觉无法言说的脆弱时期后，我终于能告诉大家了。

sentences.en: It's a sentence I always punctuate by knocking on wood.
sentences.zh: 这是一个我总会用敲木头来作为结束语的句子。

sentences.en: Ancient people did this to summon dryads, the benevolent spirits inside trees.
sentences.zh: 古人这样做是为了召唤树精，即树木中仁慈的灵魂。

sentences.en: Far from conferring the illusion of control, the sound connects me to everyone who has ever dared to hope for anything in this life with its single guarantee.
sentences.zh: 这种声音并没有赋予我控制的错觉，反而让我与每一个在这个充满唯一保证的生命中敢于抱有希望的人联系在一起。

sentences.en: Superstitions are a gentle knocking at the doorways to the future, your heart open to every possibility.
sentences.zh: 迷信是对未来之门的一次轻叩，让你的心向一切可能性敞开。

sentences.en: Letter of Recommendation
sentences.zh: 推荐信

sentences.en: Looking Out the Window
sentences.zh: 窗外眺望

sentences.en: Written by Sam Anderson
sentences.zh: 作者：Sam Anderson

sentences.en: Read by Robert Fass
sentences.zh: 朗读：Robert Fass

sentences.en: Our windows keep shrinking
sentences.zh: 我们的窗户越来越小

sentences.en: Our vision narrows and narrows
sentences.zh: 我们的视野越来越窄

sentences.en: Mine roams for much of the day in a space roughly the size of a playing card the rectangle of my phone's screen
sentences.zh: 我大部分时间都在一张扑克牌大小的空间里游荡，那就是我手机屏幕的矩形区域

sentences.en: The view through that piece of glass is not out onto the actual world but inward, down a digital depth over which I exercise near-dictatorial control
sentences.zh: 透过那块玻璃看到的景象并非外面的真实世界，而是向内，进入一个我几乎拥有独裁控制权的数字深渊

sentences.en: If I want to see a bird on my phone, I see a bird If I want to see a manatee captioned by a motivational slogan, I see that
sentences.zh: 如果我想在手机上看到鸟，我就能看到鸟；如果我想看到配有励志标语的海牛，我就能看到它

sentences.en: This means, of course, that my phone is not really a window at all
sentences.zh: 当然，这意味着我的手机根本不是一扇窗户

sentences.en: A real window is something that frames our fundamental lack of control
sentences.zh: 真正的窗户是能够框住我们根本无法控制的事物的东西

sentences.en: Windows are in this sense
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，窗户是

sentences.en: A powerful existential tool
sentences.zh: 一种强大的存在主义工具

sentences.en: A patch of the world arbitrarily framed from which we are physically isolated
sentences.zh: 一块被随意框住的、我们与之物理隔绝的世界碎片

sentences.en: The only thing you can do is look You have no influence over what you will see
sentences.zh: 你唯一能做的就是看。你对将要看到的东西没有任何影响力

sentences.en: Your brain is forced to make drama out of whatever happens to appear
sentences.zh: 你的大脑被迫从任何出现的事物中编造出戏剧性

sentences.en: Boring things become strange
sentences.zh: 无聊的事物变得离奇

sentences.en: A blob of mist balances on top of a mountain
sentences.zh: 一团雾气在山顶上保持平衡

sentences.en: Leafless trees contort themselves in slow-motion interpretive dance
sentences.zh: 无叶的树木在慢动作的现代舞中扭动身体

sentences.en: Heavy raindrops make the puddles boil
sentences.zh: 沉重的雨滴让水坑沸腾

sentences.en: These things are a tiny taste of the bigness of the world They were there before you looked They will be there after you go
sentences.zh: 这些事物只是世界宏大的一小部分。在你注视之前它们就在那里，在你离开之后它们依然会在那里

sentences.en: None of it depends on you
sentences.zh: 这一切都不取决于你

sentences.en: Sometimes what you see can be astonishing
sentences.zh: 有时你看到的东西会令人震惊

sentences.en: One day I was taking a nap in the red chair in my office when I woke up to the sound of a car crash I sat up and looked immediately out my window
sentences.zh: 有一天，我在办公室的红色椅子上打盹，被一场车祸的声音惊醒。我坐起来，立刻看向窗外

sentences.en: Across the street, in a parking lot a car had just backed into a chain-link fence
sentences.zh: 街对面的停车场里，一辆车刚刚倒车撞进了铁丝网围栏

sentences.en: The car must have been moving fast because it was in bad shape
sentences.zh: 那辆车当时一定开得很快，因为它损毁严重

sentences.en: Its hood had popped up
sentences.zh: 它的引擎盖弹了起来

sentences.en: Its windshield wipers were snapping back and forth under a perfectly clear sky and part of its bumper was sitting on the ground
sentences.zh: 在万里无云的天空下，它的雨刷器来回摆动，部分保险杠掉在地上

sentences.en: The fence was mangled bent out in exactly the shape of the car's back end
sentences.zh: 围栏被撞得扭曲变形，形状正好与车尾吻合

sentences.en: I couldn't believe I was seeing this on an otherwise ordinary weekday morning out of my office window
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信在这样一个普通的周一早晨，从我的办公室窗户看到了这一幕

sentences.en: I watched the driver get out of the car He was stocky with a shaved head He wore cargo shorts and a flannel shirt unbuttoned to expose his chest hair I disliked him immediately
sentences.zh: 我看着司机从车里出来。他身材魁梧，剃着光头。他穿着工装短裤和一件没扣扣子的法兰绒衬衫，露出胸毛。我立刻对他产生了反感

sentences.en: After a few seconds of assessing the damage he walked around the car and opened the passenger door from which a very small child scrambled out
sentences.zh: 在评估了几秒钟损失后，他绕到车边打开副驾驶门，一个非常小的孩子从里面爬了出来

sentences.en: A toddler in the front seat
sentences.zh: 前座竟然有个幼儿

sentences.en: My disdain for this man increased exponentially
sentences.zh: 我对这个男人的鄙视呈指数级增长

sentences.en: As the child ran around the parking lot the man tried to repair the damage he caused He attempted to tug the ruined fence back into place but it wouldn't move
sentences.zh: 当孩子在停车场跑来跑去时，男人试图修复他造成的破坏。他试图把毁坏的围栏拉回原位，但它纹丝不动

sentences.en: He tried to shove the fallen piece of bumper back onto his car but that only made the rest of his bumper fall off too I sat in my red chair looking out my window silently cheering
sentences.zh: 他试图把掉落的保险杠塞回车上，但这反而让剩下的保险杠也掉了下来。我坐在红椅子上看着窗外，默默地为他喝彩

sentences.en: The man tried a little harder to fix the fence He grabbed its vertical support pole which was wickedly bent and pulled against it with his full weight
sentences.zh: 男人更努力地想修好围栏。他抓住那根已经严重弯曲的垂直支撑杆，用尽全身力气拉扯

sentences.en: The pole suddenly broke and the man fell hard onto the blacktop
sentences.zh: 杆子突然断了，男人重重地摔在柏油路上

sentences.en: The entire fence fell on top of him and one of his sandals flew off and landed ten feet away on the sidewalk I think I laughed out loud
sentences.zh: 整个围栏倒在他身上，他的一只凉鞋飞了出去，落在十英尺外的人行道上。我想我笑出了声

sentences.en: This was a slapstick masterpiece It was brightening my whole day the failure of this terrible man He climbed out from under the collapsed fence
sentences.zh: 这简直是一部闹剧杰作。这个糟糕男人的失败让我的整天都明亮了起来。他从倒塌的围栏下爬出来

sentences.en: and limped back to the apartment building above the lot rubbing his elbow
sentences.zh: 揉着手肘，一瘸一拐地走回停车场上方的公寓楼

sentences.en: That, I thought, would be the end of it
sentences.zh: 我想，这下该结束了

sentences.en: The man, that villainous man was going to leave all the chaos behind for someone else to clean up It was only the middle of the morning but I imagined him sprawled out on his sofa
sentences.zh: 那个男人，那个卑劣的男人，打算把这一地狼藉留给别人去清理。虽然才上午，但我已经想象他瘫在沙发上

sentences.en: with a case of beer eating horrible snacks while his child played with fire and broken glass and battery acid near a malfunctioning electrical socket
sentences.zh: 喝着啤酒，吃着糟糕的零食，而他的孩子在故障的插座附近玩火、玩碎玻璃和电池酸液

sentences.en: But this is the power of windows They contradict your easy assumptions They scribble over your mental cartoons with the heavy red pen of reality
sentences.zh: 但这正是窗户的力量。它们反驳你轻率的假设。它们用现实那支沉重的红笔，涂抹掉你脑海中的漫画

sentences.en: The man emerged a few minutes later with some tools He got to work immediately detaching one of the fence's bent support bars and hammering it straight on the asphalt
sentences.zh: 几分钟后，男人带着一些工具出现了。他立刻开始工作，拆下围栏一根弯曲的支撑杆，在柏油路上把它敲直

sentences.en: For the next hour I watched out my window as he doggedly fixed the fence straightening and reattaching its support bars scrupulously unbending its bent chain link
sentences.zh: 接下来的一个小时里，我从窗外看着他执着地修理围栏，拉直并重新安装支撑杆，一丝不苟地掰直扭曲的铁丝网

sentences.en: He even improved it He stole a support bar from another fence farther back in the parking lot and added it to this one
sentences.zh: 他甚至改进了它。他从停车场后方的另一处围栏偷了一根支撑杆，加到了这一处上

sentences.en: Now the fence would be extra secure stronger than before impervious to damage
sentences.zh: 现在围栏会格外稳固，比以前更强，坚不可摧

sentences.en: This odious man was actually a hero I was the lazy one with my knee-jerk judgments and distant cliches my superiority from three stories up
sentences.zh: 这个可恶的男人其实是个英雄。我才是那个懒惰的人，带着膝跳反应式的判断和遥远的陈词滥调，从三层楼高的地方俯视着他
